subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: Nor is coverage established by the fact that the board of directors ratified such acts. [See Olympic Club v. Those Interested Underwriters at Lloyd's London, supra, 991 F2d at 502—policy covered corporation's imputed liability for wrongful acts of its officers and directors] [3:656 - 3:663] Reserved. (1) [3:664] Compare—entity coverage: Many D&O policies today provide “entity coverage” for certain claims made against the corporation directly, including respondeat superior liability for wrongful acts by the corporation's officers and directors. Entity coverage was developed to avoid disputes regarding allocation of defense and settlement costs where claims against insured officers and directors are joined with claims against the uninsured corporation (see discussion at ¶ 3:705 ff.). [See Continental Cas. Co. v. Anne Arundel Comm. College (4th Cir. 1989) 867 F2d 800, 801] Cross-refer: Entity coverage is discussed further in Croskey, Heeseman, Ehrlich & Klee, Cal. Prac. Guide: Insurance Litigation (TRG), Ch. 7F. f. [3:665] Claims-made coverage: D&O policies are generally written on a “claims-made” basis—i.e., they cover claims first made against the insured director or officer during the term of the policy.
